gh_api_response.interpretation: No branch protection rules defined on snowball. Autonomous merge under V3 §B2 is technically permissible (no protection blocks gh pr merge --squash), but lacks defense-in-depth (no human-review gate, no required CI checks, no force-push protection).

compatibility_rationale: snowball is the ARIA experimental branch (per CLAUDE.md ARIA Snowball policy). The branch is intentionally unprotected so the autonomous loop can squash-merge L3 PRs without operator intervention. Defense-in-depth is provided by: (a) AutoActionGate diff classifier (rejects aria-kernel/** + L3 exclusion list at materialize-time + merge-time, single SSoT), (b) circuit breaker (auto-downgrade to strict after N failures in 24h), (c) cost budget (downgrade on $/run cap), (d) cross-host lease lock (prevents concurrent merges), (e) ack-ledger HMAC signing (auto-mint is auditable + revocable), (f) materialize three-event chain (every merge has provenance).

operator_acknowledgement.acknowledgement_text: Operator approved Strategy B (full L3 autonomy) in Plan ARIA-V3 plan-mode confirmation. Branch protection absence is an accepted trade-off, mitigated by V3 architectural gates.

review_recommendation: Re-evaluate snowball branch protection after Phase B2 ships and the autonomous loop runs 7 days in shadow mode. If observed failure modes warrant tighter controls (e.g. operator-triggered emergency rollback proves non-trivial), open an ADR to add minimal branch protection (e.g. CI-check requirement) compatible with autonomous merge.
